paragraphs: The F-Type P450 is a late-cycle addition to the F-Type range, introduced as a replacement for the previous V6 S and positioned just below the R in the line-up. Like the rest of the F-Type's V8 models, it uses the AJ133 - a 5.0-litre supercharged V8 from Jaguar's Gen III AJ-V8 family, shared with the R and SVR variants. The P450 name refers to its power output in PS - a badge introduced for the 2021 model year as part of a range-wide naming restructure, bringing the F-Type's V8 offering into the same naming convention used across Jaguar's contemporary line-up. The F-Type P450 is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace AJ133 engines for every F-Type P450 on the road.

cards.body: A 5.0-litre supercharged V8 fitted to the F-Type P450 across the entire X152 generation (2013-2024). The AJ133 is a member of Jaguar's Gen III AJ-V8 family, using a cross-plane crankshaft and Eaton TVS supercharger. Timing chain tensioner and guide wear is a documented pattern on this engine family - particularly on earlier 2012-2014 examples, which were explicitly named in a US class-action lawsuit scope covering the same engine across multiple JLR models. We replace timing chains, tensioners and guides as standard on every AJ133 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The F-Type P450 uses the AJ133 V8 across its entire production run - no engine code changes occurred during this variant's life. That means compatibility for replacement or rebuild work is consistent, but sourcing a used unit still requires VIN matching to ensure the correct ECU calibration and ancillaries.
